source.title: Fulminant Brucella melitensis Infection Presenting With Severe Cholestatic Hepatitis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: A Case Report

presentation: A 54‐year‐old male engaged in livestock farming, with no history of chronic illness or medication use, presented to the emergency department with a 4‐day history of right upper quadrant tenderness, progressive jaundice, and generalized pruritus. He kept his own herd of goats and regularly consumed unpasteurized milk from these animals. His occupation entailed daily close contact with the herd within a confined barn, and contact with abortion material was considered probable, although he had not attended any parturition. There was no accompanying fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms. There was no family history of hepatic, renal, or hematologic disease, and no known relevant genetic predisposition. He reported no recent travel, no alcohol or illicit drug use, and no use of hepatotoxic, over‐the‐counter, or herbal products. On examination, prominent scleral icterus was observed. The patient was mildly lethargic, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14. Vital signs were as follows: temperature 37.8°C, blood pressure 115/70 mmHg, heart rate 92 beats/min, and respiratory rate 18 breaths/min. Abdominal examination revealed localized right upper quadrant tenderness without guarding, rebound tenderness, or Murphy’s sign. Cardiac auscultation disclosed a prominent pansystolic murmur at the mitral focus, and locomotor examination identified lumbar tenderness. The respiratory examination was unremarkable.

events.source_span: Laboratory findings on admission are summarized in Table 1.

events.detail: Marked cholestatic pattern (ALP 565 U/L, GGT 225 U/L, total bilirubin 25.1 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 23 mg/dL), severe renal failure (creatinine 11.52 mg/dL, urea 373 mg/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelets 55 x 10^9/L), and deranged coagulation (INR 1.45, fibrinogen 77 mg/dL, D-dimer 11.79 mg/L FEU)
events.source_span: The liver‐enzyme profile showed a cholestatic pattern, with a marked elevation of alkaline phosphatase (ALP; 565 U/L) and gamma‐glutamyl transferase (GGT; 225 U/L) and only mild transaminase elevation.

events.detail: Evaluation of peripheral blood smear for schistocytes and platelet aggregates
events.source_span: The peripheral blood smear demonstrated 1%–2% schistocytes, and the clinical pathologist specifically reported the absence of platelet aggregates

events.detail: 1%-2% schistocytes and absence of platelet aggregates, confirming true thrombocytopenia
events.source_span: The peripheral blood smear demonstrated 1%–2% schistocytes, and the clinical pathologist specifically reported the absence of platelet aggregates, thereby excluding pseudothrombocytopenia due to platelet clumping and confirming true thrombocytopenia.

events.detail: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP-HUS) was initially considered due to thrombocytopenia and schistocytes
events.source_span: The combination of thrombocytopenia and schistocytes initially raised concern for a thrombotic microangiopathy.

events.detail: Cross-sectional abdominal imaging to evaluate for mechanical cholestasis
events.source_span: Cross‐sectional abdominal imaging with ultrasonography and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrated no biliary dilatation or other evidence of mechanical cholestasis.

events.detail: No biliary dilatation or mechanical cholestasis; hepatosplenomegaly confirmed (liver 21 cm, spleen 14 cm) with diffuse nodular splenic parenchyma and subcentimeter lymphadenopathy
events.source_span: Cross‐sectional abdominal imaging with ultrasonography and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrated no biliary dilatation or other evidence of mechanical cholestasis. Hepatosplenomegaly was confirmed, with a liver span of 21 cm and a spleen of 14 cm.

events.detail: Secondary HLH was considered due to splenomegaly, cytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia
events.source_span: The combination of splenomegaly, cytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, and a ferritin concentration above 2000 μg/L raised the possibility of secondary HLH

events.detail: CVVHD delivered with a sepsis adsorption filter in predilution mode without systemic anticoagulation for 48 hours
events.source_span: To manage life‐threatening uremia, the patient underwent continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHD) as renal replacement therapy, delivered with a sepsis adsorption filter in predilution mode without systemic anticoagulation, for a total of 48 h over two consecutive days.

events.detail: Three sets of blood cultures and a Wright agglutination test obtained on admission
events.source_span: On the day of admission, three sets of blood cultures and a Wright agglutination test were obtained

events.detail: Empirical ceftriaxone (2 g/day intravenously) started
events.source_span: and empirical ceftriaxone (2 g/day intravenously) was started.

events.detail: Leptospirosis considered as a leading alternative diagnosis
events.source_span: leptospirosis (which characteristically presents with jaundice and AKI and is endemic in the region) was a leading alternative diagnosis.

events.detail: Positive at a titer of 1/160
events.source_span: On Day 1, the Wright agglutination test returned positive at a titer of 1/160

events.detail: Oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) and rifampin (600 mg/day) added to therapy
events.source_span: and oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) and rifampin (600 mg/day) were added.

events.detail: All three blood cultures grew B. melitensis
events.source_span: All three blood cultures subsequently grew B. melitensis, confirming the diagnosis.

events.detail: Confirmed Brucella melitensis infection based on positive blood cultures and Wright agglutination test
events.source_span: All three blood cultures subsequently grew B. melitensis, confirming the diagnosis.

events.detail: Transthoracic echocardiography to exclude infective endocarditis
events.source_span: infective endocarditis was excluded by transthoracic echocardiography in accordance with the modified Duke criteria [6]; no vegetation, valvular dysfunction, or other evidence of endocarditis was found.

events.detail: No vegetation, valvular dysfunction, or other evidence of endocarditis
events.source_span: no vegetation, valvular dysfunction, or other evidence of endocarditis was found.

events.detail: Discharged after 2 weeks of inpatient monitoring and stabilization
events.source_span: The patient was monitored as an inpatient for 2 weeks and discharged after clinical and laboratory stabilization.

events.summary: completion of antibiotic therapy and biochemical normalization
events.detail: Completed 6 weeks of doxycycline and rifampin with near-complete normalization of laboratory parameters
events.source_span: He completed the remaining course of doxycycline plus rifampin on an outpatient basis, for a total treatment duration of 6 weeks.
